source.publication: Micron Q3 FY2026 earnings / S&P Global / Goldman Sachs

description: Micron's 2026-06-24 fiscal Q3 print confirmed the memory super-cycle is real and supply-bound, NOT a sentiment bubble: 81% gross margin, entire 2026 HBM capacity fully contracted/sold out, and management guiding constraints to persist through at least 2026. Corroborating market data: Q2 DRAM contract prices +63%, NAND +75%; Goldman Sachs calls it the most severe memory shortage in 15 years (DRAM shortfall 4.9%, NAND 4.2%, HBM 5.1% for 2026), with AI infrastructure absorbing ~23% of global DRAM wafer output. This is a fundamentals-CONFIRMING counterpoint to the 06-05/late-June AI-chip selloff: while fabless/compute names (Nvidia, Broadcom) sold off on capex-peak fears, the memory IDMs printed record margins on a genuine physical shortage. Directly bullish for sector semiconductors_memory (Micron, SK Hynix, Samsung); confirms the AI-capex structural via real revenue, not guidance.
user_notes: Registered 2026-06-29 in the scan refresh. Maps to the promoted sector semiconductors_memory (gap_20260604, promoted 2026-06-04) — so it is a Pass-2 classification, not a gap update. The signal that originated the Discovery Pass ('RAM disk' case) is now a hard-fundamental confirmation. Importance for the book: it splits the 'AI selloff' into two regimes — compute/fabless under capex-peak pressure (cat_20260605) vs memory IDMs with record margins on a physical shortage. semiconductors_memory has no open movement yet but ranks as a candidate. is_priced_in 0.5: memory names already ran hard YTD, so much of the shortage is in the price; the earnings confirm staying power rather than re-rating from scratch. consensus_surprise 0.4: the shortage was well-telegraphed; the 81% margin magnitude was the beat.

review_log.evidence: The shortage has extended its duration rather than resolving: all three major HBM suppliers confirm sold-out capacity through 2026, with SK Hynix describing HBM, DRAM and NAND as 'essentially sold out' for the year, and tight DRAM supply now expected to persist BEYOND 2026. Chinese conventional-DRAM relief lands only in consumer devices, not the HBM bottleneck.
